claim: Unraid OS 7.4.0 was released 2026-11-10 with Linux kernel 6.18.60-Unraid; 7.3.5 (same day) is a maintenance release on the same kernel
Unraid installs on a USB flash drive, boots from it and loads into a root RAM file system; it runs on 64-bit x86_64 systems; OS configuration is stored on the boot drive

Unraid 7.3.0 (2026-05-12) added internal boot (ahci/mmc/nvme/USB and a few SAS drivers; optional ZFS boot pool), an onboarding wizard and TPM-based licensing; its notes say do not roll back to 7.2.6 or earlier after enabling internal boot or TPM licensing, and upgraded ZFS pool features may not import on earlier releases

Unraid's base distribution is Slackware-derived [inferred: webGUI init scripts are headed 'Init script for libvirtd on Slackware' and the boot tool has a 'slackware' case; the vendor docs do not name a base distro]

The Unraid OS updater (unRAIDServer.plg) downloads the release zip and an MD5 file from Unraid's server, compares MD5, unzips, then compares each file against .sha256 sidecar files shipped inside the same zip; no cryptographic signature check was found in the update script
Before installing, the Unraid updater moves the running bz* kernel/rootfs files to /boot/previous (one previous version kept) and then moves the new files into place; a reboot completes the update

Unraid rollback is manual: Tools > Downgrade OS restores the previous version when its files are still on the boot device (the plugin 'remove' method moves /boot/previous back and asks for a reboot); otherwise the user copies bz* files from a downloaded zip by hand; no automatic fallback after a failed boot was found
The Unraid updater ensures syslinux boot entries for 'Safe Mode (no plugins)' exist, so a user can boot without plugins after a bad plugin/update

Unraid plugins integrate directly with the OS and WebGUI; Unraid's own docs list 'full filesystem access increases security risks' and instability after OS updates as cons, and advise Docker containers for general applications

Unraid's Community Applications store is run by a moderation team that gives 'basic vetting'; submissions go through a portal with repository XML guidance, validation, scanning and review; moderators may take over abandoned apps for security fixes
Since Unraid 7.2.0 (2025-10-29) the Unraid API (GraphQL; API keys, session cookies and SSO/OIDC) is built in, and optional WebGUI login via SSO/OIDC was added; the API repository is GPL-2.0-or-later
Unraid's WebGUI plugins (dynamix) are published under GPL-2.0, while the OS itself is sold under a proprietary perpetual licence keyed to a USB GUID or (7.3+) a TPM

Unraid Starter and Unleashed licences include one year of updates, then an optional USD 36/year extension; Lime Technology supports only the two most recent public minor versions (a public beta/RC counts), so a lapsed licence stops getting security patches once its minor version goes EOL

Unraid has no shipped MCP server: a 'Work Intent: Add native MCP support to Unraid API' issue (#2024, opened 2026-06-11) is closed with no release-note mention; issue #2065 (opened 2026-08-25, open) reports a VIEWER API key with only READ_ANY can execute notification mutations; community MCP servers wrap the GraphQL API

claim: Synology's package developer guide: DSM 7.0 removed package (.spk) code signing and the Package Center keyring/trust levels (any non-Synology package gets an alert on install), and forces packages to run as a dedicated non-root user via conf/privilege, with privileged operations through 'resource workers'

Synology AI Console (DSM 7.2+) lets admins enable AI per package and per user/group, connect Amazon Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Baidu, Google AI Studio/Vertex, OpenAI or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, de-identify prompts (regex or local NER models, no full-masking guarantee) and log every request; GPU-only embedding/OCR/STT/captioning models run on Synology systems with a GPU; 16 GB RAM recommended

Synology says AI Console was deployed on more than 430,000 systems between its August 2025 launch and 2025-10-08 (vendor claim); DSM 7.3 relaxed its drive policy so 2025 model-year Plus, Value and J models accept third-party drives for installation and pool creation (M.2 pools still need the compatibility list)

DSM 7.4 adds 'DSM Agent', which turns administrators' natural-language questions into diagnostic insights, and semantic search in Synology Drive; AI Console supports local on-device LLMs and OpenAI-compatible APIs from version 1.2.0

Synology Container Manager package versions follow Docker releases (20.10.23 → 24.0.2; still 24.0.2-1707 on 2026-11-05); its Project page supports Docker Compose; 2026-05-06 added container GPU access through an NVIDIA Runtime Library package; later versions need DSM 7.4; some ARMv8 models were added

Synology product support status: 'Full' = continuous updates, 'Limited' = security updates only, 'End of Life' = no further updates; DSM 6.2 reached the end of its Extended Life Phase on 2024-10-01 (announced 2023-10-01), after release in 2018
